highlight: Traces the route of continental Europe’s first passenger railway of 1835 and ends under the vast domed railway cathedral of Antwerpen-Centraal.

name: Kusttram
highlight: The world’s longest tram line: 67 km of metre-gauge track hugging the entire Belgian coast from De Panne to Knokke, calling at 68 stops.

name: Intercity
highlight: A cross-border Intercity through the wooded Éislek and the Ourthe and Amblève valleys, one of the prettiest rail rides in the Ardennes.

name: RE 11 Mosel
highlight: The RE 11 follows the Moselle from Luxembourg into Germany, boring through the 4.2 km Kaiser-Wilhelm-Tunnel at Cochem to bypass the river’s huge loop.

name: TER
highlight: A short cross-border hop from Luxembourg’s Ville-Haute down to the old French steel town of Longwy, one of the busiest daily commuter runs into the Grand Duchy.

name: Marschbahn
highlight: Reaches the car-free island of Sylt over the 11 km Hindenburgdamm causeway of 1927, a dead-straight embankment laid across the tidal Wadden Sea.

name: TGV inOui
highlight: France’s first high-speed line, opened in 1981: the Paris–Lyon route that launched the whole TGV era, now run in under two hours.

name: TGV inOui
highlight: The 2017 Bretagne–Pays de la Loire high-speed line cut Paris–Rennes to 1 h 25 min, sending TGVs racing across Brittany at 320 km/h.

name: TGV inOui
highlight: TGV Atlantique runs Paris to the Loire estuary city of Nantes in about two hours, topping 300 km/h across the plains of the west.

name: TGV Lyria
highlight: A Lyria Euroduplex glides from Paris into Switzerland at Genève-Cornavin; the 2010 Haut-Bugey line trimmed the run to about three hours.

name: Ouigo
highlight: SNCF’s low-cost double-decker TGV, launched in 2013 with fares from €10, races Paris to Lyon at up to 300 km/h.

name: TGV inOui
highlight: France’s longest domestic TGV run: 300 km/h to Marseille, then the classic Riviera line along the Mediterranean to Nice.

name: TGV inOui
highlight: The dead-straight LGV Nord links Paris to Lille in just 62 minutes at 300 km/h, France’s fastest big-city hop.

name: Intercités
highlight: The Bourbonnais line to the Auvergne volcanoes; new Oxygène trainsets arrive from 2026 to retire its veteran Corail carriages.

name: Intercités
highlight: The cross-country POLT line, Paris-Orléans-Limoges-Toulouse, runs 713 km through the Massif Central on France’s classic north–south artery.

name: Train des Pignes
highlight: Metre-gauge “pine-cone train” climbing 151 km from Nice to Digne over some 25 tunnels and 16 viaducts, inaugurated in 1911.

name: Train des Merveilles
highlight: Spirals up the wild Roya valley past the Bronze-Age rock carvings of the Vallée des Merveilles, looping through helicoidal tunnels to Tende at 1,040 m.

name: Mont-Blanc Express
highlight: A metre-gauge mountain line under Mont Blanc, using third-rail power and a rack section to climb the Chamonix valley from Saint-Gervais into Switzerland.

name: Chemins de fer de la Corse
highlight: Corsica’s beloved “U Trinichellu” crosses the island’s granite spine, piercing the 3.9 km Vizzavona tunnel at 906 m altitude.

name: AVE
highlight: Branches off the Madrid–Levante high-speed line to reach the Costa Blanca, opened in 2013 and worked by S-112 “Pato” trainsets.

name: AVE
highlight: The first stretch of Spain’s Madrid–Barcelona line (2003), crossing the Guadalajara plateau and Ebro valley to Zaragoza in 75 minutes.

name: AVE
highlight: Leaps into Galicia through 30 tunnels, including the 8.6 km O Corno bore, then runs on down the Atlantic axis through Santiago de Compostela to the coast at A Coruña.

name: AVE
highlight: Opened in 2019, it branches off the Córdoba–Málaga line at Antequera to lift the AVE network into the foothills of the Sierra Nevada.

name: AVE
highlight: A single high-speed run tying the Mediterranean to the Costa del Sol, skirting Madrid to stitch two AVE corridors together.

name: El Transcantábrico
highlight: Spain’s first hotel-train (1983): an eight-day, metre-gauge cruise along the green Cantabrian coast from the Basque Country to Galicia.

name: Tren dels Llacs
highlight: A heritage “train of the lakes” climbing beside the Noguera Pallaresa past reservoirs and tunnels to the Pyrenean foothills.

name: El Expreso de La Robla
highlight: Retraces the historic La Robla coal railway, Spain’s longest narrow-gauge line, on a three-day luxury run between Bilbao and León.

name: Alfa Pendular
highlight: Portugal’s tilting Pendolino leans into the curves at up to 220 km/h, dropping down the Alentejo to the Algarve at Faro.

name: Intercidades
highlight: Climbs the Beira Alta line to Guarda, Portugal’s highest city at 1,056 m, on the historic Sud Express path toward the Spanish border.

name: Presidential Train
highlight: Royal-blue saloon carriages built from 1890, which once carried heads of state, now a fine-dining train up the terraced Douro wine valley.

name: Linha do Minho
highlight: Follows the Atlantic, then the Minho river, to the star-fort town of Valença, staring across the water at Spain’s Tui.

name: Linha do Oeste
highlight: A slow, winding single-track line through the vineyards and spa towns of Estremadura (Torres Vedras, Caldas da Rainha) to the Atlantic at Figueira da Foz.

name: Frecciarossa
highlight: A Frecciarossa 1000 hit 393.8 km/h on this Turin–Milan high-speed line in a 2016 test, an Italian rail speed record.

name: Frecciarossa
highlight: The 300 km/h spine of Italy. Milan–Bologna–Florence–Rome–Naples runs almost entirely on dedicated high-speed track finished in 2009.

name: Frecciarossa
highlight: South of Caserta the Freccia climbs through the Apennines to Foggia, then races across the Tavoliere plain to the Adriatic port of Bari.

name: Frecciargento
highlight: One of Italy’s longest Freccia runs: some 671 km down the Tyrrhenian coast, the tilting ETR 485 leaning through curves toward the Strait of Messina.

name: Italo
highlight: Italo was Europe’s first private open-access high-speed operator; its Alstom AGV 575 links Milan and Rome in under three hours.

name: Frecciarossa
highlight: A tilting ETR 600 Frecciarossa crosses the Po plain and Veneto from Milan to Trieste on the Adriatic, a run it took over in June 2023.

name: Ferrovia Circumetnea
highlight: A 950 mm narrow-gauge line almost encircling Mount Etna, Europe’s most active volcano, crossing black lava fields around Bronte and Randazzo.

name: Trenino Verde
highlight: At 159 km the longest tourist railway in Italy, this narrow-gauge line climbs to 868 m through the wild Ogliastra mountains to the sea at Arbatax.

name: Rittner Bahn
highlight: A metre-gauge survivor of a 1907 rack railway, its vintage tramcars glide across the sunny Renon plateau above Bolzano, the Dolomites on the horizon.

name: Circumvesuviana
highlight: The narrow-gauge line to Sorrento, opened in 1948, carries travellers past the ruins of Pompeii and Herculaneum under the shadow of Vesuvius.

name: Pelion Railway
highlight: Evaristo de Chirico’s 600 mm mountain railway on Mt Pelion curls over his iron-and-stone bridge near Milies through olive and apple groves.

name: Proastiakos
highlight: Athens’s fast electric suburban line skirts the Saronic Gulf and crosses the Corinth Canal on its run from the port of Piraeus out to Kiato, and since 2020 on along the Gulf of Corinth to Aigio.

name: Zagreb–Rijeka line
highlight: Climbs through the forested Gorski Kotar highlands, through tunnels and curves before the steep final plunge to the Adriatic at Rijeka.

name: Zagreb–Osijek line
highlight: Runs east across the flat Pannonian farmland of Slavonia to Osijek, Croatia’s fourth-largest city, on the Drava near the Hungarian border.

name: Ljubljana–Koper line
highlight: Drops nearly 500 m off the Karst plateau to the sea, twisting through tunnels and curves on the descent to Slovenia’s only seaport, Koper.

name: Podgorica–Nikšić line
highlight: Reopened to passengers after electrification in 2012, the line takes 12 tunnels and 9 bridges below the cliffs of Ostrog Monastery.

name: Sarajevo–Ploče line
highlight: Threads the plunging Neretva canyon between the Prenj and Čvrsnica massifs, then follows the river down to the Adriatic at Ploče through 106 tunnels.

name: Skopje–Bitola line
highlight: Climbs from the Vardar at Veles over the Babuna mountains on the looping Bogomila grade before dropping onto the Pelagonia plain to Bitola.

name: Skopje–Gevgelija line
highlight: Follows the Vardar south and squeezes through the Demir Kapija, the “Iron Gate” gorge, on Corridor X’s run toward Greece.

name: Pristina–Peja line
highlight: Kosovo’s sole surviving passenger service: two little diesel trains a day amble west via Klina to Peja under the Accursed Mountains.

name: Frecciarossa
highlight: Frecciarossa 1000 sets cross from Rome over the Apennines and the Po plain via Florence and Bologna to reach Venice in under four hours.

name: Transiberiana d’Italia
highlight: Italy’s “Trans-Siberian”: a heritage train over snowbound Apennine plateaus to Rivisondoli-Pescocostanzo, at 1,268 m among the country’s highest stations.

name: Ferrovia delle Meraviglie
highlight: The “Railway of Wonders” spirals up the Alps through helical tunnels and viaducts into France; wrecked in WWII, it reopened only in 1979.

name: Vinschgau Railway
highlight: Closed to passengers in 1990, this South Tyrol branch reopened in 2005 as a rural-rail success story and went fully electric in 2026.

name: Bolzano–Merano Railway
highlight: Half-hourly FLIRTs climb the Etsch valley between South Tyrol’s capital and the spa town of Merano, the 1881 line that feeds the Vinschgau reopening.

name: R16 Praha–Železná Ruda
highlight: Prague to the edge of the Bohemian Forest, ending at a station shared with Bavaria across the border; the 1877 climb to it bored the Špičák tunnel, longest in the Czech lands for 130 years.

name: Ex7 Praha–Český Krumlov
highlight: A direct express from Prague to the UNESCO town inside the Vltava’s double bend, over rails laid in 1891 to carry Schwarzenberg timber and graphite rather than tourists.

name: Plzeň–České Budějovice Railway
highlight: The rychlík between Pilsner country and Budweiser country: 136 km through the wooded south Bohemian hills via Strakonice, on rails laid in 1868.

name: Marumaru no Hanashi
highlight: A KiHa 47 dawdling along the San’in coast between Shimonoseki and Hagi, timed so the Sea of Japan fills the windows. Back running after 2025’s storm damage.

name: Summerauerbahn
highlight: The Summerauerbahn: out of Budweis, over the granite hills where Europe’s first horse-drawn railway ran, down the Mühlviertel to the Danube at Linz.

name: Šumava Railway
highlight: The Šumava forest railway: out of Budějovice, past Český Krumlov’s castle bend, along Lake Lipno and up into the Bohemian Forest at Volary.

name: Riviera Line
highlight: The Riviera on rails: Nice, Villefranche, Monaco’s covered station, Menton lemon groves and over the border to Ventimiglia. Forty minutes of Mediterranean out the right-hand window.

name: Clermont–Lyon
highlight: Across the top of the Massif Central: volcano country out of Clermont, the Gorges over Roanne, then down into the Rhône at Lyon.

name: Marseille–Briançon
highlight: The Durance valley all the way up: Aix, Sisteron’s citadel, Gap, Embrun above the lake, and the highest town in France at the buffer stops.

name: Caen–Le Mans–Tours
highlight: Normandy to the Loire without touching Paris: the cross-country line through Alençon and Le Mans that the TGV network forgot.

name: Caen–Rennes
highlight: The western way round: Saint-Lô, the Vire bocage, a glimpse of Mont-Saint-Michel country at Dol, then Rennes.

name: Reims–Dijon
highlight: Champagne to Burgundy behind the front: Châlons, Chaumont’s viaduct and the Langres plateau, four departements of France nobody flies over.

name: Metz–Strasbourg
highlight: Lorraine to Alsace under the Vosges foothills, through Sarrebourg and the Saverne gap: the eastern half of the historic Paris–Strasbourg corridor.

name: Eifelbahn
highlight: Rebuilt after the 2021 flood tore it out: Cologne into the volcanic Eifel over Gerolstein’s crags and down the Kyll gorge to Trier.

name: Südbahn
highlight: Württemberg’s Südbahn, electrified at last: Ulm’s minster to Lake Constance at Friedrichshafen, then along the shore to Lindau island.

name: RE5 Berlin–Rostock
highlight: Berlin to the Baltic in one seat: the Mecklenburg lake district at Neustrelitz and Waren, then Rostock and the ferries.

name: Cagliari–Sassari
highlight: The Sardinian main line: three hours up the island’s spine through Oristano and the Campidano plain. Most visitors never know Sardinia has a main line.

name: Alvia Madrid–Salamanca
highlight: Over the Guadarrama by high-speed line, then across Castile to the golden sandstone of Salamanca in well under two hours.

name: Zaragoza–València (via Teruel)
highlight: The emptiest main line in Spain: five hours via Teruel, a provincial capital with no direct Madrid train, through ochre gorges to the Mediterranean.

name: Midland Main Line
highlight: St Pancras’s own main line: Leicester, Derby and Chesterfield’s crooked spire, into Sheffield under the Bramall Lane floodlights.

name: Hull Trains
highlight: An open-access original: Hull’s own train to London since 2000, off the East Coast racetrack at Doncaster and over the Ouse into Paragon station.

name: Cardiff–Portsmouth
highlight: Wales to the Solent the slow, lovely way: the Severn Tunnel, Bath’s crescents, Salisbury’s spire and the harbour at Portsmouth.

name: Cambrian Line
highlight: Birmingham to the Irish Sea over the Cambrian Mountains: Welshpool, the Talerddig summit cutting, Machynlleth and the estuary into Aberystwyth.

name: Liverpool–Norwich
highlight: England corner to corner: five hours and a bit through Sheffield, Nottingham and the Fens, the longest all-stops cross-country ride in the country.

name: Dublin–Rosslare
highlight: DART territory then the wild bit: Killiney bay, Wicklow’s cliff ledge above the sea, Wexford’s quays, and the Europort at the end.

name: Kust till kust-banan
highlight: Coast to coast across Småland: Borås, the glass country around Växjö, and Kalmar castle on the Baltic at the far end.

name: REX Wien–Sopron
highlight: Vienna into Hungary the old imperial way: Wiener Neustadt, the Ödenburg plain, and GySEV’s green-and-yellow home town of Sopron.

name: Railjet Vienna–Bregenz
highlight: The full west-bound railjet: Salzburg, Innsbruck, the Arlberg tunnel and out at the Bodensee. Austria end to end in one train.

name: Gäubahn IC
highlight: The Gäubahn intercity: over the Rhine at Schaffhausen, past the Bodensee’s back country and down the Neckar cuttings into Stuttgart.

name: Avant Málaga–Sevilla
highlight: Andalusia’s own high-speed shuttle: Málaga to Seville via Córdoba’s mezquita city in two hours, on the S-104 sets built for exactly this.

name: Celta
highlight: The only train across the Portugal–Spain border in the north: down the Minho, over the Valença bridge, into Galicia. Two countries, one ticket, 2 h 35.

name: IC Kraków–Przemyśl
highlight: The old Galician main line east: Kraków, Tarnów, Rzeszów and the fortress town of Przemyśl, last stop before Ukraine.

name: Paris–Granville Line
highlight: Paris to the Channel the Norman way: through Dreux and Argentan to the walled harbour of Granville, no TGV in sight.

name: Nantes–Quimper
highlight: South Brittany strung together: Redon, the Gulf of Morbihan at Vannes, Lorient and the Odet valley into Quimper.

name: RE7 Bern–Luzern
highlight: The Emmental cut-through: cheese country and covered bridges between the federal city and the lake at Lucerne, hourly.

name: IC61 Basel–Interlaken
highlight: Basel to the Bernese Oberland in one seat: Olten, Bern, then the lakeside crawl past Thun and Spiez to Interlaken under the Eiger.

name: Train Suite Shiki-shima
highlight: JR East’s champagne-gold cruise train: four days from Ueno through Tōhoku and under the Seikan Tunnel to Hokkaido, in suites with cypress baths. Japan’s hardest train ticket.

name: Golden Eagle Trans-Siberian Express
highlight: The Trans-Siberian done as a private hotel on wheels: fourteen days Moscow to Vladivostok with en-suite cabins, a bar car and stops the scheduled Rossiya cannot make.

name: Schlossbergbahn Graz
highlight: Up the Schlossberg through the trees since 1894, from the Mur embankment to the clock tower above Graz’s red roofs.

name: Heidelberg Bergbahnen
highlight: Two funiculars stacked end to end: a modern car to the castle, then 1890s wooden carriages on up to the Königstuhl summit, Germany’s longest funicular climb.

name: Dresden Standseilbahn
highlight: From Loschwitz villa streets to the Weißer Hirsch heights since 1895, sister to the suspension railway one valley over.

name: Funicular de Artxanda
highlight: Bilbao’s 1915 escape hatch: three minutes from the Casco Viejo edge to the Artxanda ridge and the whole Guggenheim skyline at your feet.

name: Johnstown Inclined Plane
highlight: Built after the 1889 flood so Johnstown could flee uphill: one of the world’s steepest vehicular inclines, still hauling cars up Yoder Hill.

name: Frecciargento
highlight: A tilting ETR 485 runs Rome to the heel of Italy’s boot via Foggia, Bari and Brindisi, reaching baroque Lecce in the Salento.

name: InterCity Slovenija
highlight: SŽ’s tilting Pendolino links Slovenia’s two largest cities along the 1840s Austrian Southern Railway, weaving down the Sava and Savinja valleys.

name: Narita Express
highlight: Twin sets from Yokohama and Shinjuku couple at Tokyo Station, then run as one red-and-black E259 through the Sobu tunnels out to Narita Airport.

name: Thunderbird
highlight: Since the 2024 bullet-train extension it sprints from Osaka up the wild western shore of Lake Biwa to Tsuruga, Hokuriku’s new shinkansen gateway.

name: Haruka
highlight: Kansai Airport’s purple-and-white express, covering 99 km from Kyoto’s temples out across the bay to the man-made island runway.

name: Kaiji
highlight: Chuo Line express using the E353’s active tilt to swing through the mountain-walled Katsura valleys up to the vineyard capital of Kofu.

name: Hokuto
highlight: Diesel tilting express curving 319 km around Uchiura Bay past the volcanoes Usu and Komagatake, linking Sapporo with old Hakodate.

name: Ozora
highlight: Crosses Hokkaido’s wild interior, the Hidaka range and the Sekisho tunnels, to the crane marshes of Kushiro on the far Pacific coast.

name: Enoden
highlight: Century-old seaside interurban that skims Shonan’s surf beaches and brushes past house walls; its Kamakurakokomae crossing is an anime shrine.

name: Oigawa SL Kawane-ji
highlight: Vintage C11 steam locomotives haul old coaches up the Oi River valley: the same railway that runs Japan’s Thomas the Tank Engine trains.

name: Isumi Railway
highlight: Restored 1960s diesel railcars trundle past rice paddies and spring nanohana blossoms through the rural heart of the Boso Peninsula.

name: Shimakaze
highlight: Kintetsu’s luxury Shimakaze (double-decker observation cars, leather saloons and a café) glides to the pearl bays and shrines of Ise-Shima.

name: Laview
highlight: Seibu’s radical Laview, with a huge curved windscreen and yellow living-room windows, climbs from Ikebukuro into the Chichibu mountains.

name: Fujisan View Express
highlight: Steep little Fujikyu line to Lake Kawaguchi, its wide panorama windows framing Mt Fuji rising straight ahead.

name: Yakumo
highlight: JR West’s new 2024 tilting 273 series takes the Hakubi line’s passes to Izumo, home of Japan’s oldest grand shrine.

name: Ibusuki no Tamatebako
highlight: Split black-and-white treasure box train that puffs a cloud of mist from its doors, rounding Kinko Bay to the hot-sand baths of Ibusuki.

name: Aso Boy!
highlight: Family sightseeing express with a panorama cab and play areas, zig-zagging the Tateno switchback into the vast Mt Aso caldera.

name: Watarase Keikoku Railway
highlight: Open-sided torokko trolleys wind up the Watarase gorge on the old Ashio copper-mine line, ablaze with wisteria and autumn maple.

name: ITX-Saemaeul
highlight: Tilting-comfort intercity that succeeded the storied Saemaul-ho, still running the full 442 km Gyeongbu spine from Seoul to Busan.

name: ITX-Cheongchun
highlight: Double-deck 180 km/h EMU on the Youth Line, racing up the Bukhan River to the lake city of Chuncheon, home of dak-galbi.

name: Mugunghwa-ho
highlight: Korea’s beloved everyman Rose of Sharon train: cheap reserved seats and rattling coaches taking the slow road from Seoul to Busan.

name: KTX-Eum Jungang Line
highlight: The rebuilt Jungang line, run through since December 2024: EMU-260 sets from Seoul past Confucian Andong and Gyeongju’s royal tombs, down the Donghae line to Bujeon in Busan in 3 h 56.

name: KTX-Eum Jungbu Inland
highlight: Korea’s newest inter-city railway, finished through to Mungyeong in November 2024: EMU-260 sets past Chungju and the Suanbo hot springs to the old post road town under Mungyeong Saejae.

name: DMZ Peace Train
highlight: Tourist train relaunched in 2026, running to Dorasan: the last station on the line before North Korea, at the fenced edge of the DMZ.

name: Tze-Chiang Limited Express
highlight: Taiwan’s flagship Teng-Yun EMU3000, with a business-class car, curving down the wild Pacific east coast from Taipei to Taitung.

name: Taroko Express
highlight: Japanese-built TEMU1000 tilting train carving through the Yilan cliffs and tunnels from Taipei to the marble gorge country of Hualien.

name: Neiwan Line
highlight: Hakka-country branch line climbing from Hsinchu into the hills to the old timber and coal town of Neiwan, revived as a heritage day-trip.

name: Jiji Line
highlight: Taiwan’s cherished 1922 branch line through betel-palm country and a camphor-tree green tunnel, reopened in 2026 after a landslide closure.

name: Shen’ao Line
highlight: Short coastal branch to Badouzi, the Taiwan station nearest the sea, where rainbow-painted railcars run beside the wave-cut Shen’ao arch.

name: Raja Tehran–Tabriz
highlight: Iranian leg of the Tehran–Istanbul Trans-Asia Express, whose onward run once floated the whole train across Turkey’s Lake Van on a rail ferry.

name: Raja Tehran–Isfahan
highlight: Links the capital to the old Safavid capital and its UNESCO-listed Naqsh-e Jahan Square, shadowing Iran’s still-unfinished first high-speed line.

name: Raja Tehran–Bandar Abbas
highlight: One of Iran’s longest single-train rides: ~1,290 km across the central desert past Yazd to the Strait of Hormuz, completed when the Bafq link opened in 1995.

name: Yüksek Hızlı Tren (YHT)
highlight: Turkey’s second high-speed line (2011) cut Ankara–Konya from over 10 hours to under two, racing across the Anatolian steppe past salt-pan Lake Tuz.

name: Yüksek Hızlı Tren (YHT)
highlight: Turkey’s longest domestic high-speed line, 406 km over 11 tunnels and 6 viaducts, replaced a 12-hour conventional slog to Sivas with under three hours.

name: İzmir Mavi Treni
highlight: One of Turkey’s last classic ’Blue Train’ sleepers: 883 km overnight across western Anatolia via Eskişehir while the parallel high-speed line stays years off.

name: Doğu Ekspresi
highlight: Turkey’s cult 1,365 km trans-Anatolian sleeper to the snowy Caucasus frontier at Kars; social-media fame makes seats sell out weeks ahead.

name: Israel Railways · Beersheba line
highlight: A fast double-tracked run to the Negev’s capital, tracing the Ottoman military railway thrown down in 1915 to supply the WWI Sinai front.

name: Israel Railways · Coastal line
highlight: Israel’s busiest rail corridor follows the Mediterranean shore from the Galilee coast through Haifa Bay to Tel Aviv, with trains every 15–30 minutes.

name: SAR East Train
highlight: Saudi Arabia’s first railway, the 1951 Dammam–Riyadh line built under King Abdulaziz, still crosses the Eastern desert and the vast Al-Ahsa oasis.

name: SAR North Train
highlight: At 1,242 km Saudi Arabia’s longest passenger line strikes north from Riyadh across the Great Nafud desert to Qurayyat near the Jordanian border.

name: Talgo Intercity
highlight: Cairo–Alexandria is the oldest railway in Africa and the Middle East (1854–56); since December 2022 it has been worked by Spain’s Talgo 230 trainsets.

name: Hejaz Railway (heritage)
highlight: Lawrence of Arabia’s Ottoman pilgrimage railway; heritage trains still run north from Amman via Zarqa, and a Hejaz steam loco fired up again in 2025 after 40 years.

name: Al Atlas
highlight: The everyday intercity linking Morocco’s imperial cities (Rabat, Meknès and Fès) up to eight times a day, parallel to but separate from the Al Boraq high-speed line.

name: Al Atlas
highlight: A surviving direct classic train after Al Boraq took the coastal corridor in 2018: still running Tanger Ville to Fès with no change, via the Rif foothills.

name: Al Atlas Oriental
highlight: The slow ’Oriental’ run passes the Taza Gap between the Rif and Middle Atlas to reach Oujda on the sealed Algerian frontier.

name: SNCFT Grandes Lignes
highlight: Tunisia’s metre-gauge trunk line runs frequent air-conditioned expresses down the Sahel coast past the great Roman amphitheatre of El Jem to Sfax.

name: Accra–Tema Shuttle
highlight: Revived in July 2022, the shuttle turns a peak-hour road crawl of up to two hours into a roughly one-hour rail run between Ghana’s capital and its main port at Tema.

name: Sitarail Voyageurs
highlight: The lone survivor of the once-famous Abidjan–Ouagadougou train: a weekly Burkina-only service revived in November 2023 between the two biggest cities.

name: Transgabonais
highlight: Gabon’s only passenger railway climbs from the Atlantic at Owendo through equatorial rainforest past Lopé National Park to Franceville, running largely overnight.

name: Matadi–Kinshasa
highlight: Reopened in September 2025 after a five-year landslide closure, now worked at weekends by KiHa 183 railcars shipped from Japan, relinking Kinshasa to its Atlantic port.

name: Shosholoza Meyl Limpopo
highlight: North to the Limpopo overnight, up through Polokwane and the bushveld to Musina, on a line that reached the copper town in 1914 and the river crossing to Zimbabwe in 1927.

name: Shosholoza Meyl Komati
highlight: The old Delagoa Bay line to the Mozambique border, out through Pretoria and Witbank and down the escarpment past Nelspruit to the lowveld, overnight in a little over twelve hours.

name: Shosholoza Meyl Trans-Natal
highlight: Down the Natal main line overnight: out of Johannesburg at half past eight, over the Drakensberg escarpment in the dark, into Durban and the Indian Ocean at seven.

name: Shosholoza Meyl
highlight: The last affordable long-distance sleeper in South Africa: an overnight economy train across the Free State Highveld and Stormberg to the Indian Ocean at East London.

name: Nampula–Cuamba
highlight: One of Africa’s great budget rail adventures: a full day across the baobab-studded bush of Niassa, carriages packed with traders and sacks of produce.

name: Sena Line
highlight: A subsidised lifeline up the Zambezi valley, crossing the 3.7 km Dona Ana bridge, once the longest railway bridge in Africa, from the port of Beira to the Tete coalfields.

name: Kampala–Mukono commuter
highlight: Revived in December 2024 on the century-old metre-gauge ’Lunatic Line,’ it beats Kampala’s notorious gridlock into the city for a few thousand shillings.

name: Fianarantsoa–Côte Est (FCE)
highlight: Madagascar’s rainforest lifeline: 67 bridges and 48 tunnels down a 1,100 m escarpment past waterfalls; villages survive by loading bananas and coffee onto the train.

name: Trans Lémurie Express
highlight: Reopened in December 2023 after ~30 years shut by cyclone damage, its rosewood-trimmed cars climb through the highlands to the spa town of Antsirabe.

name: Eritrean Railway
highlight: Pre-war Italian Mallet steam locos still claw up 3.5% grades and switchbacks 2,300 m between the Red Sea and Asmara: one of the great colonial mountain railways.

name: Port Sudan–Atbara
highlight: The first railway to reopen after Sudan’s civil war (December 2024): a fortnightly desert lifeline from the Red Sea across Nubian scrub to the Nile junction at Atbara.

name: SJ Snabbtåg
highlight: SJ’s tilting X2000 links Stockholm with Malmö and the Øresund gateway at up to 200 km/h. Sweden’s flagship fast run down the Southern Main Line.

name: SJ Snabbtåg
highlight: Fast SJ trains climb the East Coast Line along the Gulf of Bothnia’s shore to the old timber city of Sundsvall.

name: SJ Nattåg
highlight: SJ’s sleeper rolls out of Stockholm at night and wakes among the snow-clad fells of Jämtland at the Åre ski resort.

name: Norrtåg
highlight: A rare passenger run through Norrland’s forests joining two northern university cities near the head of the Gulf of Bothnia.

name: Roslagsbanan
highlight: Sweden’s last commercial narrow-gauge railway (891 mm), still running through Stockholm’s leafy northern suburbs out to rural Kårsta.

name: Öresundståg
highlight: Rolls off Sweden’s West Coast Line and over the 8 km Øresund Bridge, plunging into the Drogden tunnel to reach Copenhagen.

name: DSB InterCity
highlight: DSB’s long haul up Jutland, crossing the Great Belt Fixed Link, to Aalborg, gateway to Denmark’s north.

name: DSB InterCity
highlight: Runs west to Esbjerg, Denmark’s North Sea port and the historic embarkation point for steamers and emigrants to Britain.

name: Østfoldbanen
highlight: Vy’s RE20 traces the Østfold Line down the east shore of the Oslofjord toward the Swedish border at Halden.

name: Gjøvikbanen
highlight: Climbs out of Oslo through the deep Nordmarka forest and over Hadeland to Lake Mjøsa at Gjøvik.

name: Vestfoldbanen
highlight: RE11 starts at Eidsvoll, calls at the airport, then runs down the fjord’s west side through Tønsberg, Norway’s oldest town, to industrial Grenland.

name: Lokaltog L1
highlight: Crosses Oslo end to end: the 1872 Drammen Line’s original alignment out to Spikkestad at one end, Norway’s first railway of 1854 to Lillestrøm at the other.

name: Regiontog RE10
highlight: Threads Oslo from Drammen, calls at the airport, then follows the east shore of Mjøsa, Norway’s largest lake, north to the Olympic town of Lillehammer.

name: Flytoget
highlight: Norway’s fastest train at 210 km/h, running out to Gardermoen through the 14.6 km Romeriksporten tunnel under the Romerike ridge.

name: InterCity 25
highlight: Finland’s Main Line north to the Gulf of Bothnia: the double-deck IC25 is now the fastest to Oulu, with ex-Russia Allegro sets running alongside as Pendolino Plus since late 2025.

name: VR InterCity
highlight: A double-deck InterCity east along the Karelian line to Joensuu, gateway to Finland’s forested North Karelia.

name: VR InterCity
highlight: The Savo line threads through Finland’s lake district to Kuopio, water rarely out of sight; InterCitys continue north to Iisalmi and Kajaani.

name: VR Night Train
highlight: Finland’s northernmost railhead: an overnight car-carrier sleeper above the Arctic Circle to the fells of Ylläs and Levi.

name: Elron
highlight: Estonia’s busiest intercity run: orange Stadler FLIRTs linking Tallinn with Tartu, the country’s ancient university city.

name: Elron
highlight: Runs east to Narva on the Russian frontier, where two medieval castles face off across the border river.

name: Elron
highlight: A rural FLIRT ride south through Estonia’s forests and bogs to the lakeside hill town of Viljandi.

name: Vivi
highlight: The historic Riga–Dünaburg line to Daugavpils, Latvia’s second city, hard by the Lithuanian and Belarusian borders.

name: Vivi
highlight: Vivi’s new PESA railcars reach the twin border town of Valga/Valka, split between Estonia and Latvia, now a link in the Baltic capitals chain.

name: Vivi
highlight: A once-daily run reborn in 2017, crossing Courland to Liepāja, the windswept Baltic port and former Tsarist naval base.

name: LTG Link
highlight: Hourly express between Lithuania’s two largest cities along a segment of the old St Petersburg–Warsaw Railway.

name: LTG Link
highlight: LTG Link’s longest domestic haul, crossing Samogitia to Klaipėda, Lithuania’s only seaport on the Baltic.

name: LTG Link
highlight: The first direct Vilnius–Riga train in decades, restored in 2023, reconnecting two Baltic capitals via Šiauliai and Jelgava.

name: LTG Link
highlight: For years the Baltics’ only rail gateway to the rest of Europe. Vilnius to Warsaw through the Suwałki Gap, changing trains at Mockava.

name: Vande Bharat Express
highlight: India’s third Vande Bharat: a fully-AC self-propelled set gliding the Mumbai–Ahmedabad corridor at up to 130 km/h.

name: Vande Bharat Express
highlight: India’s second Vande Bharat, launched 2019 to carry pilgrims 655 km from Delhi to the Vaishno Devi base town of Katra.

name: Vande Bharat Express
highlight: South India’s first Vande Bharat (India’s 5th), linking Chennai, Bengaluru’s tech hub and the palace city of Mysuru.

name: Vande Bharat Express
highlight: Crosses the Chenab Rail Bridge: 359 m above the river, the world’s highest railway arch bridge, taller than the Eiffel Tower.

name: Gatimaan Express
highlight: India’s first 160 km/h train: the “Speedy” express dashes Delhi to Jhansi via Agra’s Taj and the fort city of Gwalior.

name: Vivek Express
highlight: India’s longest train journey: 4,154 km and roughly 75 hours from Assam’s tea country to the subcontinent’s southern tip.

name: Palace on Wheels
highlight: India’s original luxury train (1982): a week-long Rajasthan circuit in carriages styled on the private saloons of the maharajas.

name: Deccan Odyssey
highlight: Maharashtra’s answer to the Palace on Wheels: a blue-liveried luxury rake looping the Konkan coast to the Ajanta and Ellora caves.

name: Kangra Valley Railway
highlight: The world’s longest 2 ft 6 in narrow-gauge line, curling 164 km below the snow-capped Dhauladhar range on nearly 1,000 bridges.

name: Tejas Express
highlight: India’s first train run by a separate operator, IRCTC, rather than the Railways: with onboard hosts and automatic payouts for delays.

name: Duronto Express
highlight: An all-AC, near-non-stop “Duronto” linking India’s two biggest cities across the central heartland in about 27 hours.

name: Swarna Shatabdi
highlight: The Swarna Shatabdi day train (1994) speeds from the capital to the Golden Temple city of Amritsar in a shade over six hours.

name: Subak Raftar
highlight: A fast daytime intercity up Pakistan’s historic Main Line 1, sprinting Lahore to Rawalpindi across the Chenab and Jhelum rivers.

name: Parabat Express
highlight: Runs Dhaka to Sylhet through the emerald tea gardens and forested hills of Srimangal, Bangladesh’s brew capital.

name: Sundarban Express
highlight: Now races Dhaka to Khulna over the 6.1 km Padma Bridge, whose rail deck opened in 2024 to slash the journey to the southwest.

name: Banalata Express
highlight: Bangladesh’s flagship no-stop intercity, crossing the 4.8 km Jamuna “Bangabandhu” Bridge on its Dhaka–Rajshahi dash.

name: Yal Devi
highlight: Sri Lanka’s Northern Line express: its tracks to Jaffna, torn up during 25 years of civil war, were relaid and reopened in 2015.

name: Lào Cai Sleeper
highlight: Overnight metre-gauge sleeper up the Red River valley to Lào Cai, the mountain gateway to the terraced rice slopes of Sapa.

name: Hai Phong Line
highlight: French-built in 1902, this metre-gauge line still links Hanoi to Vietnam’s great northern port through the Red River delta.

name: Da Lat Railway
highlight: The last working stub of the French cog railway to Da Lat: 7 km of heritage track from a 1938 Art Deco station to Trại Mát.

name: Maeklong Railway
highlight: At Mae Klong the train noses through Talat Rom Hup, the market whose stallholders whisk their awnings off the rails as it passes.

name: Eastern Line
highlight: Bargain 3rd-class ordinary trains rattle to the frontier at Ban Khlong Luek. Thailand’s rail gateway to Cambodia and Angkor.

name: KTM ETS
highlight: The world’s fastest metre-gauge service at 140 km/h, running the peninsula’s west coast to the Thai border at Padang Besar.

name: Jungle Railway
highlight: The nicknamed Jungle Railway crosses Malaysia’s rainforested interior past Taman Negara, from Gemas up to Tumpat near the Thai border.

name: Argo Parahyangan
highlight: The scenic conventional climb over the Priangan highlands and tall Cikubang viaduct: the leisurely rival to the Whoosh bullet line.

name: KRL Commuterline
highlight: Java’s first electrified inter-city commuter outside Jakarta, gliding past the 9th-century Prambanan temples between two royal cities.

name: Yangon–Mandalay Express
highlight: Myanmar’s 1889 British-built rail spine, now covered in about 10 hours by new air-conditioned DEMU expresses.

name: PNR Commuter
highlight: A surviving stretch of the century-old Manila–Legazpi main line, its ex-Japanese railcars trundling through Quezon’s coconut country.

name: Cornish Riviera Express
highlight: The daytime flyer to Britain’s far south-west since 1904, racing 300 miles past Dartmoor and along the wave-battered Dawlish sea wall to Penzance.

name: South Wales Main Line
highlight: GWR’s flagship South Wales express; Hitachi bi-modes drop off the 25 kV wires west of Cardiff and switch to diesel for the last dash to Swansea.

name: Great Western Main Line
highlight: Brunel’s original 1841 main line: billiard-table levels from Paddington to Didcot, then a 1 in 100 fall through the 3 km Box Tunnel, said to face the sunrise on his birthday.

name: Avanti West Coast
highlight: Italian-built tilting Pendolinos lean into the curves of the West Coast Main Line, holding 125 mph where an upright train would have to brake.

name: Avanti West Coast
highlight: Fast tilting Pendolinos finish at Liverpool Lime Street, opened 1836 and one of the world’s oldest grand terminus stations still in daily use.

name: Avanti West Coast
highlight: Traces the pioneering 1838 London and Birmingham Railway, the first great trunk line driven into the capital, from Euston to England’s second city.

name: LNER
highlight: Japanese-designed Azuma bi-modes sprint the East Coast Main Line out of King’s Cross (1852) to reach Leeds in a little over two hours.

name: LNER
highlight: Azuma expresses hold 125 mph down the East Coast Main Line, coming over the Tyne into Newcastle on Robert Stephenson’s High Level Bridge.

name: CrossCountry
highlight: Britain’s longest direct train: one Voyager grinding 695 miles and nearly 40 stops from Aberdeen on the North Sea to Plymouth on the Channel.

name: Kyle of Lochalsh Line
highlight: One of the world’s great scenic railways, blasted through Torridonian rock for 82 miles from Inverness to the Skye ferry pier at Kyle of Lochalsh.

name: Far North Line
highlight: Britain’s most northerly line, a lonely 4-hour run to Wick that swings far inland on the Lairg Loop to dodge the deep Highland sea firths.

name: Heart of Wales Line
highlight: A 121-mile request-stop ramble through empty Mid Wales, crossing the castle-like 13-arch Knucklas Viaduct where trains halt only if you flag them down.

name: Cambrian Coast Line
highlight: Clings to the Mid-Wales shore on mostly single track, rumbling across the half-mile timber Barmouth Viaduct over the Mawddach estuary.

name: North Wales Coast Line
highlight: The old Irish Mail route to the Dublin ferries, crossing Robert Stephenson’s Britannia Bridge to Anglesey and skirting the walls of Conwy Castle.

name: North Yorkshire Moors Railway
highlight: One of the world’s busiest steam heritage lines, climbing Stephenson’s 1836 route over the moors to Goathland, Hogsmeade in the Harry Potter films.

name: Severn Valley Railway
highlight: Sixteen miles of preserved Great Western branch line tracing the River Severn, crossing the water on the graceful iron span of Victoria Bridge.

name: Bluebell Railway
highlight: The world’s first preserved standard-gauge passenger railway, running vintage steam through the Sussex Weald without a break since 1960.

name: West Somerset Railway
highlight: Britain’s longest standard-gauge independent heritage railway: 22¾ miles of steam from the Quantock Hills down to the Bristol Channel shore at Minehead.

name: Vale of Rheidol Railway
highlight: Narrow-gauge steam grinding 200 m uphill from the sea at Aberystwyth to the wooded gorge of Devil’s Bridge: the last steam line British Rail ever ran.

name: InterCity
highlight: Iarnród Éireann’s diesel railcars strike west across the boggy Irish Midlands, crossing the Shannon at Athlone to the Atlantic city of Galway.

name: InterCity
highlight: Leaves the Dublin–Cork main line at Limerick Junction, a curious station where trains long had to reverse, before the final run to the Shannon at Limerick.

name: InterCity
highlight: The old Midland Great Western route from Dublin Connolly over the drumlin lakelands to Sligo, W. B. Yeats’s country beneath flat-topped Ben Bulben.

name: InterCity
highlight: Curves south-west from Dublin through medieval Kilkenny to Waterford, Ireland’s oldest city, founded by Vikings on the tidal River Suir.

name: DART
highlight: Ireland’s only electrified railway, running around Dublin Bay from the Howth peninsula past Killiney’s Irish Riviera to Greystones since 1984.

name: Belfast–Derry Line
highlight: Michael Palin called the Coleraine–Derry run one of the world’s most beautiful; the train skims the Atlantic strand below cliff-top Mussenden Temple.

name: Dartmoor Line
highlight: The first line reopened under Britain’s Restoring Your Railway plan, bringing regular trains back to Okehampton on the edge of Dartmoor half a century after closure.

name: Šargan Eight
highlight: A 760 mm loop climbing 300 m through 22 tunnels and 5 bridges in a literal figure-eight to gain height.

name: Belgrade–Niš Line
highlight: Serbia’s first main line squeezes through the Grdelica Gorge on stone viaducts. Corridor X’s slowest link, now rebuilding for 200 km/h.

name: EuroCity “Sava”
train: SŽ series 342 electric locomotive · EuroCity coaches
highlight: The EC “Sava” restored a direct Zagreb–Ljubljana run, and since June 2025 extends once a week onward to Pula for the first time in 30 years.

name: Bucharest–Constanța InterCity
highlight: Romania’s fastest domestic run crosses the Danube on Anghel Saligny’s 1895 bridge before new EMUs race on to the Black Sea.

name: Ionian Coast Line
highlight: Sicily’s east coast end to end: out of Messina along the Ionian shore below Taormina, past Etna at Giarre and Acireale into Catania, then the salt flats and Augusta’s bay to Siracusa. Complete.

name: Tren de la Fresa
operator: Fundación de los Ferrocarriles Españoles · Renfe
highlight: Hostesses in 1920s dress hand out strawberries aboard replica carriages on Spain’s second-ever railway, opened in 1851.

name: El Canfranero
highlight: Reopened in June 2025 after two years of works, the line climbs to Europe’s grandest abandoned border station, shut since a 1970 bridge collapse.

name: R11 Costa Brava Line
highlight: Regional trains skirt Costa Brava cliffs near the French border before Portbou, terminus of the line completed in 1878.

name: Linha do Vouga
train: Metre-gauge diesel railcar · heritage wooden-carriage train (summer Sat.)
highlight: Portugal’s last surviving metre-gauge line still carries commuters, and a vintage wooden-carriage special every summer Saturday.

name: Ligne des Pyrénées
highlight: Four daily trains climb past Foix’s castle and Ax-les-Thermes to Latour-de-Carol, where three different rail gauges meet.

name: Montreux–Rochers-de-Naye Railway
highlight: Climbs 1,700 m from Lake Geneva’s shore to a marmot-filled Alpine garden in under an hour, on Abt rack track dating to 1892.

name: Wengernalpbahn
highlight: The world’s longest continuous cogwheel railway links Lauterbrunnen and Grindelwald over Kleine Scheidegg, under the Eiger’s north face.

name: Furka Cogwheel Steam Railway
highlight: Volunteer-run steam locomotives claw over the 2,160 m Furka Pass past the Rhône Glacier on track abandoned when the base tunnel opened in 1982.

name: Brienz Rothorn Bahn
highlight: A 25% steam rack line, Europe’s highest unelectrified railway, climbs from Lake Brienz to a 2,244 m summit in an hour.

name: Chur–Arosa Line
train: RhB Ge 4/4 II electric multiple unit
highlight: Seventy curves and the record-setting 1914 Langwieser Viaduct carry hourly trains from Chur up into the ski resort of Arosa.

name: Achenseebahn
highlight: Europe’s oldest still-working steam cog railway: its four 1889 locomotives haul open carriages up to the turquoise Achensee.

name: Schafbergbahn
highlight: Austria’s steepest steam rack railway climbs 1,190 m in 40 minutes to a summit overlooking eleven Salzkammergut lakes.

name: Pinzgauer Lokalbahn
highlight: A 760 mm-gauge valley line follows the Salzach past Hohe Tauern peaks to Krimml, ending beneath Austria’s highest waterfall.

name: Zillertalbahn
train: Modern diesel railcar · steam-hauled heritage train
highlight: A working 760 mm-gauge valley railway that still runs steam trains alongside its half-hourly regular service to Mayrhofen.

name: Čierny Hron Forest Railway
highlight: One of Europe’s last steam-worked forestry railways: its branch to Dobroč runs straight through the middle of a village football pitch.

name: Štrba–Štrbské Pleso Rack Railway
highlight: Slovakia’s only cog railway climbs 430 vertical metres up a 15% rack gradient into the High Tatras on hybrid EMUs delivered in 2021.

name: Trenčín Electric Railway (TREŽ)
highlight: One of Europe’s oldest surviving interurban tramways: 1950s narrow-gauge electric railcars still shuttle up to a Habsburg-era spa town.

name: Skagen Line (Skagensbanen)
highlight: Runs to Denmark’s northernmost station through dune plantations to the sand-blown artists’ town where two seas meet at Grenen.

name: Jokioinen Museum Railway
highlight: The last stretch of Finland’s once-extensive 750 mm network, run by volunteers with steam engines from Finnish, German, Soviet and Belgian builders, veterans of the country’s vanished narrow-gauge lines.

name: Porvoo Museum Railway
highlight: Summer museum trains out of Helsinki: a 1950s Dm7 “flat-hat” railbus leaves the main line at Kerava for the 1874 branch to Porvoo’s wooden old town.

name: IR 90 Geneva–Brig
highlight: The IR 90 follows the whole north shore of Lake Geneva, then turns up the Rhône between towering valley walls: Lavaux vineyards, the castles of Aigle and Sion, and the Simplon railhead at Brig.

name: TransPennine Express
highlight: Coast to coast across northern England: Liverpool to Manchester, over the Pennines by way of Huddersfield and Leeds, then up the East Coast Main Line to the Tyne.

name: Intercités
highlight: The great southern transversale, Atlantic to Mediterranean with no Paris detour: Garonne vineyards, Carcassonne’s citadel and the Sète lagoons on the slow way round to Marseille.

name: Intercity Riviera
highlight: Down the Po plain to Genoa, then the full Italian Riviera westward: tunnel after tunnel between the mountains and the sea to San Remo and the French border at Ventimiglia.

name: Frecciarossa Adriatica
highlight: Frecciarossas run the whole Adriatic seaboard: high-speed to Bologna, then the classic 1872 Adriatica within sight of the sea past Rimini, Ancona and Pescara to Bari.

name: Chopin
highlight: The Chopin sleeper has linked Vienna and Warsaw since at least the 1980s, slipping through the Moravian Gate by night and finishing down Poland’s CMK fast line into the capital before six.

name: Gulbene–Alūksne Narrow Gauge Railway (Bānītis)
highlight: The only regularly operating narrow-gauge passenger railway left in the Baltic states, rattling twice daily through Vidzeme’s forests.

name: Aukštaitija Narrow Gauge Railway (Siaurukas)
highlight: Weekend survivor of a 750 mm network that once ran 68 km to Panevėžys, now trundling summer tourists out to Rubikiai lake.

name: Carpathian Tram (Vyhoda Forest Railway)
train: TU8P / TU6D diesel locomotive · open carriages
highlight: Ukraine’s last working forest railway, built in 1890 to haul Carpathian timber, now carries tourists up the Mizunka valley past waterfalls.

name: Zaslonov Children’s Railway
train: TU2 / TU7 diesel locomotive · narrow-gauge coaches
highlight: A working 750 mm railway through Chelyuskintsy Park operated entirely by schoolchildren training as drivers, conductors and dispatchers.

name: Lillafüred Forest Railway
highlight: Narrow-gauge line through the Bükk mountains via two tunnels and two viaducts, opened for timber and now Hungary’s best-loved forest train.

name: Szilvásvárad Forest Railway (Szalajka Valley)
highlight: Hungary’s busiest narrow-gauge railway: a steep timber line up the Szalajka valley to a waterfall, now carrying 300,000-plus riders a year.

name: Jindřichův Hradec–Nová Bystřice Narrow Gauge
highlight: South Bohemia’s narrow-gauge survivor, rescued by a new operator in 2026 after the original company’s 2022 bankruptcy nearly ended the line.

name: Train 1900 (Fond-de-Gras Heritage Railway)
train: Steam & diesel locomotives (former Prince Henri Railway stock)
operator: AMTF (Association des Musées et Tourisme Ferroviaires)
highlight: Vintage steam trains rattle through Luxembourg’s old iron-mining Minett region on track first laid in 1874 to move ore and miners.

name: Bieszczady Forest Railway
train: Px48 steam locomotive · Lyd2 diesel locomotive
highlight: Poland’s highest narrow-gauge line, a former logging railway that now carries over 150,000 riders a year into the Bieszczady wilderness.

name: Waterford & Suir Valley Railway
highlight: Narrow-gauge trains follow the tidal River Suir on the trackbed of an 1878 mainline, running alongside the Waterford Greenway cycle path.

name: Sauschwänzlebahn (Wutach Valley Railway)
train: Class 52 / 93 steam locomotive · heritage diesel railcars
highlight: Germany’s only spiral railway tunnel: a 1,700 m loop at Stockhalde lets the line climb the Black Forest by circling back over itself.

name: Chemin de Fer de la Baie de Somme
train: 130T steam locomotive (Cail · Haine-Saint-Pierre) · Belle Époque carriages
operator: Association du Chemin de Fer de la Baie de Somme
highlight: Belle-Époque steam trains skirt the Somme estuary’s tidal salt marshes, with locomotives running round their own train at each terminus.

name: Chemin de Fer du Bocq
train: Vintage SNCB railcar · heritage diesel locomotives
highlight: Three tunnels and five stone viaducts pack into the Bocq valley on one of Belgium’s most dramatically engineered branch lines.

name: Museumstoomtram Hoorn–Medemblik
train: Preserved steam locomotives (SHM fleet) · vintage carriages
highlight: A steam tram dating from 1887 still crosses North Holland’s polders and tulip fields between Hoorn and the old Zuiderzee port of Medemblik.

name: Talyllyn Railway
train: Preserved 0-4-0T / 0-4-2T steam locomotives (Talyllyn, Dolgoch, Edward Thomas)
highlight: The world’s first railway saved by volunteers, in 1951: its Victorian steam engines still cross Dolgoch Viaduct into the Fathew valley.

name: Romney, Hythe & Dymchurch Railway
highlight: Marketed as the world’s smallest public railway, its steam expresses still get local schoolchildren to class along Romney Marsh.

name: Selketalbahn (Harz Narrow Gauge)
train: Class 99.7 Mallet steam locomotive · heritage coaches
highlight: Metre-gauge Mallet steam locomotives still double-head trains out of Alexisbad on this Harz valley line, opened for timber and ore in 1887.

name: Arlberg Railway
highlight: Eight hours Zurich to Vienna on Austria’s only east–west mountain mainline: the Trisanna gorge, Wiesberg Castle and a 1,310 m summit in the 10.2 km Arlberg tunnel.

name: Al Ándalus
highlight: A rolling Belle Époque palace whose 1929 sleeping cars once carried the British court from Calais to the Riviera: now easing from Seville to Madrid in seven days.

name: Belmond Royal Scotsman
highlight: Just 40 guests aboard mahogany-panelled Pullmans that cross the Forth Bridge outbound and stable each night in Highland sidings.

name: TGV inOui
highlight: Paris to Barcelona in 6 h 39 min, diving under the Pyrenees through the 8.3 km Perthus tunnel at the Spanish border.

name: Berlin-Warszawa-Express
highlight: Six EuroCitys a day across the North European Plain, with the cult WARS dining car serving pierogi between the Oder and the Vistula.

name: Brenner Railway
highlight: Munich to Verona over the first railway across the main Alpine crest (1867), still topping the open pass at 1,371 m: no summit tunnel, just a border station.

name: Cremallera de Núria
highlight: The only way to roadless Núria: Abt rack rails climbing 1,000 vertical metres through the Freser gorges to a sanctuary at 1,964 m.

name: Lötschberger
highlight: The 1913 mountain line the base tunnel made optional. Felsenburg spirals, a 14.6 km summit tunnel, then the Bietschtal bridge on a ledge above the Rhône.

name: Intercity Notte Rome–Palermo
highlight: Europe’s last train on a ship: the sleeper is split at Villa San Giovanni and floated across the Strait of Messina before breakfast.

name: Frecciarossa Paris–Milan
highlight: Italy’s 300 km/h flagship on French rails, using the 13.7 km Fréjus tunnel of 1871: back since April 2025 after a 19-month landslide closure.

name: Tauern Railway
highlight: Franz Joseph’s 1909 crossing of the Hohe Tauern: stone viaducts up the Gastein spa valley to an 8.4 km tunnel at 1,226 m.

name: Isle of Man Steam Railway
highlight: Victorian Beyer Peacock tanks of 1874 still haul their original carriages down 25 km of 3 ft gauge to the island’s southern tip.

name: Coastal Classic
highlight: Skirts the bore-tide flats of Turnagain Arm, then climbs past Spencer Glacier into country no road reaches.

name: Belmond Hiram Bingham
highlight: Belmond’s navy-and-gold Pullman to Machu Picchu, with brunch, a pisco bar and citadel entry folded into the fare since 2003.

name: Train de Charlevoix
highlight: Runs 140 km wedged between Laurentian cliffs and the St. Lawrence, at times just metres from the tide.

name: Sudbury–White River
highlight: Canada’s last Budd RDC mainline train will flag-stop anywhere along 484 km of roadless Canadian Shield.

name: Winter Park Express
highlight: Amtrak’s revived ski train climbs more than 1,100 m through 28 tunnels and spills skiers out steps from Winter Park’s lifts.

name: Canyon Spirit
highlight: Three dome-car days Denver to Salt Lake City: the Continental Divide inside the 10 km Moffat Tunnel, the Colorado River through canyons no road enters, Moab’s red rock, then Castle Gate and Soldier Summit.

name: Strasburg Rail Road
highlight: Chartered in 1832, America’s oldest continuously operating railroad still steams through Lancaster County’s Amish farmland.

name: Mountaineer
train: EMD GP38 diesels, dome & open cars
highlight: Follows the 1875 Maine Central grade up Crawford Notch, creeping across the curved Frankenstein Trestle high above the Saco.

name: Royal Gorge Route
highlight: Rides the canyon won in the 1879 “Royal Gorge War”, the Arkansas River alongside and a suspension bridge 291 m overhead.

name: St. Kitts Scenic Railway
highlight: The last railway of the West Indies loops the island on a 1912–26 sugar-cane line, ridden in double-deck open-top cars.

name: Maria Fumaça de Tiradentes
highlight: Baldwin steam locomotives have worked this 76 cm-gauge line ever since Emperor Pedro II opened it in 1881.

name: Trem do Vinho
highlight: A 1941 steam engine ambles 23 km through the Serra Gaúcha wine country to a soundtrack of tarantellas and popping corks.

name: Blue Mountains Line
highlight: Climbs from near sea level to 1,017 m at Katoomba through a UNESCO-listed maze of sandstone cliffs and eucalypt canyons.

name: Savannahlander
highlight: Sixty-year-old railmotors take two unhurried days to cover 424 km from coastal rainforest to the 1910 gold-rush railhead at Forsayth.

name: Electric Tilt Train
highlight: The world’s fastest narrow-gauge train: it set Australia’s rail speed record of 210 km/h in 1999 and still tilts through cane country at 160 km/h.

name: Canberra Xplorer
highlight: The only passenger train to Australia’s capital: three Xplorer railcars a day take the 1914 branch past the wind farms above Lake George.

name: Cockle Train
highlight: Rides Australia’s oldest steel-railed public route, opened in 1854 with horse haulage to link Murray riverboats to the sea.

name: Te Huia
highlight: Restored intercity rail between Waikato and Auckland in 2021 after a 20-year gap, and went seven-days-a-week in 2025.

name: Southern Line
highlight: From Muizenberg the rails run on a False Bay sea wall so close to the surf that winter swells spray the carriage windows at Kalk Bay.

name: Nanyuki Safari Train
highlight: Crosses the equator on its final approach to Nanyuki, where Mount Kenya’s 5,199 m massif fills the carriage windows.

name: Luanda–Malanje Express
highlight: Angola’s oldest railway, silenced for decades by civil war, reopened end-to-end in 2011 after a Chinese-led rebuild of all 424 km.

name: Van Gölü Ekspresi
highlight: Ends 1,267 km from Ankara at a ferry slip on Lake Van, where wagons bound for Iran are floated across Turkey’s largest lake.

name: HaEmek (Jezreel Valley) Line
highlight: Rebuilt on the 1905 Ottoman Hejaz alignment, it ends at Beit She’an: about 120 m below sea level, among the world’s lowest stations.

name: Tehran–Shiraz Night Train
highlight: Completed only in 2009, the overnight run leaves Tehran at dusk and descends at dawn past Marvdasht, the plain of Persepolis, into Shiraz.

name: North Borneo Railway
train: Wood-fired 1954 Vulcan 2-6-2 steam locomotive, colonial-green carriages
highlight: A 1954 Vulcan Foundry engine burning jungle firewood retraces the 1896 British North Borneo line: the only passenger railway corridor on Borneo.

name: Araku Vistadome
train: Glass-roofed Vistadome coach on the Visakhapatnam–Kirandul train
highlight: India’s first Vistadome coach (2017) climbs the Eastern Ghats to Shimiliguda, long the country’s highest broad-gauge station at 996 m.

name: Sethu Express (Boat Mail)
train: ICF sleeper rake behind WAP-4 electric
highlight: Heir to the 1914 Boat Mail that fed the Ceylon ferry, it now reaches Rameswaram island over India’s first vertical-lift sea bridge, opened 2025.

name: Marine Liner
train: JR 5000 series + 223-5000 series EMU with double-deck panorama car
highlight: Every half hour it rides the lower deck of the 13.1 km Great Seto Bridge: the Seto Inland Sea’s only rail crossing, strung across five islands since 1988.

name: Sanriku Railway Rias Line
highlight: Japan’s longest third-sector railway follows 163 km of tsunami-rebuilt coast; the final gap closed in 2019, eight years after the 2011 wave.

name: Tsugaru Stove Train
train: 1948 Ohafu 33 coaches with coal daruma stoves, DD350 diesel
highlight: Aboard Japan’s northernmost private railway, attendants grill squid on pot-belly coal stoves while blizzards bury the Tsugaru plain outside.

name: Hue–Da Nang Heritage Train
train: Restyled vintage coaches with saloon car (HD1–HD4)
highlight: Launched in 2024 on the 1906 colonial mainline, it eases over the Hai Van Pass with clouds above and fishing fleets directly below the rails.

name: Taksaka
train: KAI New Generation stainless-steel executive & luxury coaches
highlight: Java’s flagship day train links the capital and the sultan’s city in six hours, skirting volcanoes beyond Cirebon and Purwokerto.

name: Jiayang Steam Train
train: C2-class 762 mm steam locomotive, wooden open-window coaches
highlight: One of the world’s last everyday steam railways: C2 engines built for 1950s coal pits still haul villagers past rapeseed terraces for pocket change.

name: Jaffar Express
highlight: Pakistan’s longest through service tops the Bolan Pass at Kolpur (1,790 m), then follows the Indus corridor 1,632 km to the gate of the Khyber.

name: Royal Railway Northern Line
highlight: Cambodia’s 1932 French rice line, silenced by war and revived in 2018, ambles past Tonle Sap paddies to Battambang’s art-deco station.

name: Eurostar
highlight: The original Channel Tunnel service to the EU capital takes St Pancras to Bruxelles-Midi in under two hours, city centre to city centre.

name: Eurostar
highlight: A single train from St Pancras to Amsterdam Centraal since 2018: under the Channel, across Flanders and over the Dutch polders in about four hours.

name: TGV / ICE
highlight: A Franco-German alliance since 2007: 320 km/h on the LGV Est to Lorraine, then the Saar and Rhine-Main into Frankfurt, TGV and ICE sharing the run.

name: Alvia
highlight: Off the 1992 Madrid–Seville high-speed spine, a gauge-changing Talgo carries on through sherry country to the Atlantic at Cádiz.

name: Borealis
highlight: Amtrak’s May 2024 daytime run up the Mississippi from Chicago through Milwaukee and Wisconsin’s river bluffs to the Twin Cities.

name: Aoniyoshi
highlight: A 2022 salon train styled on Nara’s Tenpyō court art, linking Osaka, the old capital Nara and Kyoto with a library bar and a sweets counter.

name: Snälltåget
highlight: A private summer sleeper down through Sweden, over the Öresund bridge past Copenhagen and across Denmark to Berlin, outlasting the state night trains.

name: Desert Express
train: TransNamib lounge & sleeper cars, GE diesels
highlight: A slow luxury run from the highland capital down the escarpment to the Atlantic, with dune walks as the Namib shifts from gold to coastal fog.

name: Wuppertal Schwebebahn
highlight: The world’s oldest electric suspension railway, hanging from a steel frame above the Wupper river since 1901, a monorail that never stopped commuting.

name: Odontotos Rack Railway
highlight: An 1896 rack line climbs 700 m up the sheer Vouraikos gorge to Kalavryta, through tunnels and along ledges cut above the torrent.

name: Voralpen-Express
highlight: Hourly cross-country trains link the abbey city of St. Gallen with lakeside Lucerne across the pre-Alps, taking in the Wattwil moorland, the Rapperswil lake dam and the Rothenthurm high bog.

name: Cremallera de Montserrat
highlight: A rack railway climbing the serrated massif to the Benedictine monastery at 720 m: the pilgrims’ way to Catalonia’s black Madonna since 1892.

name: SL Yamaguchi
train: D51 steam with retro Series 35 4000 coaches
highlight: A pacific steam locomotive has hauled this special up the Yamaguchi line to the little castle town of Tsuwano, the “Kyoto of San-in”, since 1979.

name: Fairy Queen Express
train: 1855 Fairy Queen steam locomotive, heritage saloon
highlight: Hauled by the 1855 Fairy Queen, the world’s oldest working steam locomotive, on a heritage run from Delhi out to the tiger country around Alwar.

name: Chemin de fer de La Mure
highlight: Reopened in 2021, this cliffside metre-gauge line hangs on ledges and viaducts high above the turquoise Monteynard reservoir in the Isère.

name: Petit Train de la Rhune
highlight: A 1924 wooden cog train grinds up to the 905 m Basque summit of La Rhune, past pottok ponies and griffon vultures, with the Bay of Biscay spread out below.

name: Beijing–Tianjin Intercity
highlight: China’s first high-speed line, opened for the 2008 Olympics: 350 km/h across the North China Plain, capital to port city in half an hour.

name: Shanghai–Chengdu HSR
highlight: The great east–west artery takes in Nanjing, Wuhan and the Three Gorges country, reaching Sichuan’s capital from the coast in a single day.

name: Hangzhou–Huangshan HSR
highlight: Dubbed China’s most beautiful high-speed line, it slips through tea hills and water towns from West Lake to the granite of Yellow Mountain.

name: Guiyang–Chongqing HSR
highlight: Almost entirely bridge and tunnel, this 2018 line vaults the karst gorges of Guizhou to join two of the mountain south-west’s biggest cities.

name: Lanzhou–Chongqing Railway
highlight: Twenty years in the building through the folded Qinling ranges: hundreds of tunnels that finally gave Gansu a fast way down to the Yangtze.

name: Sarajevo–Maglaj line
highlight: North out of Sarajevo through the Bosna gorge and past Zenica’s steelworks to Maglaj, the surviving stub of the 1947 youth railway to the Sava.

name: Palaiofarsalos–Kalambaka
highlight: The branch to the monasteries in the sky: from the junction at Palaiofarsalos across the Thessalian plain to Kalambaka, beneath the sandstone pillars of Meteora. Athens trains connect here; no through service runs.

name: Shosholoza Meyl Trans-Karoo
train: Class 6E electric & diesel with sleeper cars
highlight: The classic Trans-Karoo run: a night and a day across the semi-desert heart of South Africa from the Highveld gold city down to Table Bay.

name: Central Line
highlight: The German-built Central Line of 1914, a metre-gauge marathon from the Indian Ocean across the plateau to Kigoma on Lake Tanganyika.

name: Baku–Tbilisi–Kars
highlight: The Silk Road revived: opened in 2017, it closes the last gap from the Caspian across the Caucasus to Turkey, a rail bridge between Asia and Europe.

name: Grand Trunk Express
train: LHB sleeper & AC coaches, WAP-7 electric
highlight: Running since 1929, the “GT” hauls down the spine of India through Bhopal and Nagpur to Chennai: 2,180 km in a day and a half.

name: Mandalay–Lashio
train: Myanmar Railways diesel with upper-class coaches
highlight: The Shan hill line crawls up from Mandalay to inch across the Gokteik viaduct: a 1900 American-built steel trestle 100 m above the gorge.

name: Gotthard Panorama Express
train: SBB panorama coaches & lake paddle steamer
highlight: A paddle steamer up Lake Lucerne, then the 1882 Gotthard line’s spirals and the Wassen church seen thrice. Summer only, once daily, seat surcharge.

name: AVE Madrid–Oviedo
highlight: The 2023 Variante de Pajares pierced the Cantabrian wall with a 25 km base tunnel, cutting Asturias’ link to Madrid to about three hours.

name: Alvia Madrid–Badajoz
highlight: High speed reached long-isolated Extremadura in 2022, passing the Roman city of Mérida to the Portuguese border at Badajoz.

name: Tren de la Muerte
highlight: Bolivia’s notorious “Death Train” rattles east from Santa Cruz through Jesuit mission country and the Chiquitano dry forest to the Brazilian frontier.

name: Bosfor Express
highlight: The overnight heir to the Orient Express, crossing the Thracian plain from Istanbul over the Bulgarian border to Sofia as the berths are made up.

name: Albula Railway
highlight: The UNESCO Albula line spirals through helical tunnels and sweeps over the six-arch Landwasser Viaduct, a curved stone bridge running straight into a cliff, on its climb to St. Moritz.

name: Montenvers Railway
highlight: A rack railway since 1908, climbing from Chamonix to a balcony above the Mer de Glace, France’s largest glacier, under the Drus and the Grandes Jorasses.

name: Mont-Blanc Tramway
highlight: France’s highest railway grinds up the flank of Mont Blanc to the Nid d’Aigle at 2,372 m, where the climbers’ route to the summit begins.

name: Schynige Platte Railway
highlight: Vintage 1914 cars grind up an Abt rack to a 2,000 m ridge, with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau lined up across the valley and an alpine garden at the top.

name: Genoa–Casella Railway
highlight: A metre-gauge mountain tram that climbs straight out of central Genoa over three Apennine valleys to the village of Casella, sea views at its back.

name: Nevada Northern Railway
highlight: America’s best-preserved steam-era short line: the “Ghost Train of Old Ely” still runs its 1910 locomotives out of a National Historic Landmark copper yard.

name: Campos do Jordão Railway
highlight: Brazil’s highest railway climbs the Serra da Mantiqueira to the mountain resort of Campos do Jordão at 1,743 m, a metre-gauge line electrified since the 1920s.

name: Zig Zag Railway
highlight: A 19th-century engineering marvel in the Blue Mountains: trains reverse down a rock-cut Z of sandstone viaducts that once carried the main western line off the plateau.

name: AVE Madrid–Murcia
highlight: High speed reached the Segura in December 2022, running Madrid to Murcia via Cuenca and Albacete on a new elevated approach into the palm-country capital.

name: Le Mastrou (Vivarais)
highlight: A metre-gauge steam survivor climbing the granite gorge of the Doux from the Rhône at Tournon to the chestnut country of Lamastre, hauled by 1903 Mallet engines.

name: Chiemsee-Bahn
highlight: The world’s oldest steam tram still in service, an 1887 green Krauss engine that shuttles down to the Chiemsee jetty for the boat to Ludwig II’s island palace.

name: Monte Generoso Railway
highlight: A rack line from the shore of Lake Lugano to a 1,704 m summit whose Mario Botta “Fiore di pietra” lookout takes in the Alps from Monte Rosa to the Apennines.

name: Great Central Railway
highlight: Britain’s only double-track heritage main line, where two steam expresses can pass at speed just as they did on the last main line built towards the Continent.

name: Keighley & Worth Valley Railway
highlight: The branch that starred in the 1970 film “The Railway Children”, steaming up the Brontë moors past Haworth to the mill village of Oxenhope.

name: Kingston Flyer
highlight: A vintage steam service on the old Southland line by Lake Wakatipu, its 1920s Ab Pacific and wooden cars a survivor of New Zealand’s golden age of rail.

name: Himsagar Express
highlight: From the Himalayan foothills at Jammu to the very tip of India at Kanyakumari: about 3,785 km through a dozen states, one of the country’s longest single journeys.

name: Frecciarossa Milan–Reggio Calabria
highlight: The red arrow’s longest domestic run: the length of Italy from Milan down the Tyrrhenian coast to the Strait of Messina at Reggio Calabria.

name: Nightjet Vienna–Rome
highlight: Board in Vienna after dinner, cross the Carinthian Alps and the Venetian plain by night, and wake rolling into Rome, a sleeper between two imperial capitals. From Villach south it runs coupled with the Munich portion as one train.

name: Aurora Winter Train
highlight: The winter run north across frozen Alaska flag-stops for bush residents between Anchorage and Fairbanks, often with the northern lights overhead.

name: TGV inOui
highlight: Races down the Rhône on the LGV Méditerranée, then rides the 2017 Montpellier bypass, the first new stretch of French high-speed line in a decade, to the edge of the Camargue.

name: TGV Lyria
highlight: Via the LGV Rhin-Rhône to the Swiss border at Basel, then along the Aare to Zürich. Paris to Switzerland’s largest city in almost exactly four hours.

name: ICE
highlight: Germany’s busiest long-distance axis, the length of the country from the Elbe to the Isar via Hanover, the Fulda gap and Nuremberg.

name: ICE
highlight: Down the Rhine-Neckar to Mannheim and up into the Swabian capital: a hard-worked spine of the south-west ICE network.

name: Railjet
highlight: Bavaria to the Danube capital along the Westbahn, past Salzburg’s fortress and the baroque abbeys of Upper Austria.

name: EIP Pendolino
highlight: Southwest across the Polish plain via Łódź to Lower Silesia’s handsome market city of Wrocław, threaded with its hundred bridges.

name: Shanghai–Hangzhou HSR
highlight: A 45-minute dash from the metropolis to West Lake, the willow-lined water garden that has drawn Chinese poets for a thousand years.

name: Koralmbahn
highlight: Austria’s game-changer of December 2025: the 33 km Koralm Tunnel cuts Graz–Klagenfurt from nearly three hours to 45 minutes, forging a new Baltic–Adriatic high-speed axis.

name: ICE
highlight: The high-speed link binding Belgium to the Rhineland: past Liège’s soaring Calatrava station and over the language border at Aachen, Charlemagne’s capital, at 300 km/h.

name: Mittenwaldbahn
highlight: Munich to the Tyrol over the Karwendel: the electrified 1912 Mittenwaldbahn climbs from Garmisch through Alpine meadows and horseshoe curves to the Seefeld saddle before dropping into Innsbruck.

name: EuroCity Allgäu
highlight: Electrified in 2020 to speed the Munich–Zürich EuroCitys across the Allgäu past baroque abbeys and Alpine foothills to the island station of Lindau on Lake Constance.

name: Schneebergbahn
highlight: Austria’s highest railway: the red Salamander cog train grinds 1,200 vertical metres from Puchberg to the Hochschneeberg terminus at 1,795 m, the Alps’ balcony over the Vienna basin.

name: Wachaubahn
highlight: Keeps to the north bank of the Danube through the UNESCO Wachau: apricot orchards and terraced vineyards past Dürnstein, where Richard the Lionheart was once held for ransom.

name: Wendelsteinbahn
highlight: Bavaria’s oldest high-mountain railway of 1912 racks up from Brannenburg through tunnels and 25% grades toward the Wendelstein’s summit cave, observatory and panorama over the Inn valley.

name: České dráhy Express
highlight: A winding cross-country run to the grand colonnades of Karlovy Vary, the Bohemian spa where Goethe, Beethoven and half of Europe’s royalty took the waters.

name: Erzbergbahn
highlight: The “Semmering of the ore”: a heritage line over the 1,204 m Präbichl pass under the terraced Erzberg, the ochre iron mountain worked for over 1,300 years.

name: Oravița–Anina Railway
highlight: The “Banat Semmering” of 1863. Romania’s first mountain railway spirals through 14 tunnels and over 10 viaducts up the Aninei gorges, a masterwork of Habsburg engineering.

name: Oslo–Göteborg
highlight: The busiest cross-border run in Scandinavia: down Norway’s Østfold Line to the frontier at Kornsjø, then through Dalsland’s forests and lakes to Sweden’s second city; a new fast line is planned to halve the time.

name: Oslo–Stockholm
highlight: Two Scandinavian capitals across the forests and lakes of Värmland, via Kongsvinger and Karlstad on Lake Vänern: a near-five-hour run that new open-access operators are racing to cut.

name: Pustertalbahn
highlight: Follows the Puster Valley below the Dolomites from the Brenner line at Fortezza past Bruneck and the Three Peaks, crossing into Austria at Innichen to run on to Lienz in East Tyrol.

name: Salzkammergutbahn
highlight: Austria’s lake district by rail: from Attnang-Puchheim along the Traunsee past the imperial spa of Bad Ischl to the shore opposite Hallstatt, the picture-postcard village mirrored in its emerald lake.

name: Meråkerbanen
highlight: Up the Stjørdal valley from the Trondheim fjord to the Swedish border at Storlien: freshly electrified in 2024, the northern rail gateway between Norway and Sweden toward Östersund.

name: Treno Gottardo
highlight: The everyday Gotthard panorama train: hourly IRs over the 1882 mountain line’s spiral tunnels, no surcharge, from Basel or Zürich to Locarno’s palms.

name: Train de l’Aubrac
highlight: One daily train across the empty heart of France: over Garabit’s red Eiffel viaduct, the Truyère gorges and the Causses down to the Med. Six hours, change at Neussargues.

name: Ligne des Horlogers
highlight: The Watchmakers’ Line: out of Besançon and up the Doubs gorges to 1,000 m Jura plateaus, crossing into Switzerland at Le Locle for watch-capital La Chaux-de-Fonds.

name: Fichtelbergbahn
highlight: Saxon narrow-gauge steam, every day of the year: 750 mm VII K locomotives hauling green coaches 238 m uphill to Oberwiesenthal, Germany’s highest town.

name: Usedomer Bäderbahn
highlight: The imperial spa line: along Usedom’s beaches from Züssow over the Peene bridge to Ahlbeck’s pier, then across the border into Świnoujście.

name: Tarka Line
highlight: Along the Taw through Henry Williamson’s Tarka the Otter country: Devon’s surviving branch line winding from Exeter’s cathedral city to Barnstaple.

name: Hel Peninsula Line
highlight: A railway down a sandbar: 34 km along the Hel spit, at points 200 m wide, open Baltic one side and lagoon the other. Packed solid every Polish summer.

name: Bastia–Calvi
highlight: The Trinighellu’s Balagne arm: inland from Bastia to Ponte-Leccia, then down to a beach-hugging crawl from Île-Rousse to Calvi’s citadel.

name: InterCity
highlight: Across the midland bogs and Mayo’s drumlin country to Clew Bay: Ireland’s western rails since 1866, with Croagh Patrick rising past the buffer stops.

name: Midland Main Line
highlight: St Pancras’s own intercity: the Midland Main Line under Barlow’s great arch, up through Bedford and Leicester to Nottingham, Britain’s last classic trunk to join the atlas.

name: Great Eastern Main Line
highlight: “Norwich in 90”: East Anglia’s main line across Constable country with its all-new Swiss-built FLIRT fleet. A whole English region in one green run.

name: Highland Main Line
highlight: Over Druimuachdar Pass at 452 m, the highest main line in Britain, threading the Cairngorms from the capital to the Highland capital.

name: West Highland Line to Oban
highlight: The West Highland Line’s other arm: splitting at Crianlarich for Loch Awe, Kilchurn Castle’s ruin and the Hebrides ferry port of Oban.

name: Welsh Marches Line
highlight: The great spine outside England’s trunk lines: Cardiff to Manchester up the castle-studded Welsh border through Abergavenny, Ludlow and Shrewsbury.

name: InterCity
highlight: Ireland’s longest ride: off the Cork line at Mallow and west past Killarney’s lakes to Tralee, with Kerry and the Atlantic at the end of the rails.

name: Brighton Main Line
highlight: Victorian London’s dash to the sea, once home of the all-Pullman Brighton Belle, and still under the hour from Victoria to the pier and the Lanes.

name: Edinburgh–Glasgow Express
highlight: Scotland’s busiest corridor since 1842: four electric expresses an hour between its two great cities over the Falkirk high route.

name: Hope Valley Line
highlight: Straight through the Peak District: Edale, Kinder Scout and the Hope valley between England’s steel and cotton cities. The hikers’ line.

name: InterCity
highlight: Into Finnish Lakeland by the tunnel-heavy Jämsä gorge cutoff, to Alvar Aalto’s university city among a thousand lakes.

name: South Western Main Line
highlight: Waterloo’s main line to the sea: Winchester’s cathedral close, Southampton’s ocean-liner docks, Bournemouth sands and the Jurassic Coast at Weymouth.

name: Cumbrian Coast Line
highlight: England’s forgotten coastal railway: the Irish Sea one side, the Lakeland fells the other, all the way round from Hadrian’s city to shipbuilding Barrow.

name: InterCity
highlight: Fourteen direct ICs a day to Finland’s sunniest city, down the Ostrobothnian flats to Vaasa and the UNESCO Kvarken archipelago.

name: Borders Railway
highlight: The Waverley Route reborn: Britain’s longest railway reopening in a century (2015), winding out of Edinburgh to Walter Scott’s Abbotsford.

name: Dalabanan
highlight: To Dalarna, Sweden’s folklore heart: Lake Siljan, Leksand’s midsummer poles and the Vasaloppet town of Mora, where the Inlandsbanan begins.

name: Conwy Valley Line
highlight: From the pier at Llandudno up the Conwy gorge into Snowdonia’s slate mountains, meeting the Ffestiniog steam trains at Blaenau: coast to crag in an hour.

name: Jūrmala Line
highlight: Latvia’s beach train: across the Lielupe to the villas and pines of Jūrmala’s resort strip, then the bog boardwalks of Ķemeri national park.

name: Western Rail Corridor
highlight: The Western Rail Corridor, reopened in 2010 after 34 years: north from Limerick through Ennis and the stone-walled edge of the Burren to Galway Bay, west of the Shannon the whole way and never near Dublin.

name: Tyne Valley Line
highlight: One of the world’s first cross-country railways (1838), shadowing Hadrian’s Wall from the Tyne to the Solway, the Roman frontier out the window.

name: InterRegio
